title.en: Contour segment orientation, closure, and endpoints
title.zh: 等值线段方向、闭合与端点

summary: Roll to nearest start, orient by signed polygon test, normalize an exact closure marker, and retain selected terminal vertex

capability: Contour segment orientation, endpoint parsing, and closure normalization
Roll a contour segment to the nearest start, orient it by a signed polygon test, remove and restore an exact repeated-start closure marker, and retain the selected terminal vertex.
operation: contour segment orientation and endpoint parsing
ordered planar vertices plus optional start/end and clockwise choice -> oriented selected vertices
discovery.model: Discrete contour parsing with a signed polygon orientation test, exact closure normalization, and a corrected inclusive endpoint; no contour reconstruction.
discovery.geometry: Planar contour vertices in caller length units; orientation is inferred from the polygon rather than from a field.
discovery.boundary: Default retains all vertices after normalizing an exact first/last closure marker; the explicit nearest end is inclusive and suppresses automatic re-closing; non-exact repeated endpoints and general topology policies are excluded.

identity.relation: Contour segment orientation, closure, and endpoints
identity.direction: Declared inputs to ordered selected vertices with exact closure normalization
identity.definition: Roll to nearest start, orient by signed polygon test, normalize an exact closure marker, and retain selected terminal vertex
identity.model: Source contour parsing with exact closure normalization and inclusive endpoint
identity.boundary: Default restores one exact closure edge; explicit nearest end is inclusive without automatic re-closing
assumptions: Finite planar segment with meaningful polygon orientation
An exact first/last duplicate denotes a closure marker

inputs.name: flpoints
inputs.constraints: Finite supplied ordering; exact first/last duplicate denotes closure

inputs.name: end_coord
inputs.description: Nearest terminal coordinate included in output
inputs.constraints: Terminal vertex retained; no interpolated crossing; presence suppresses automatic re-closing

outputs.name: segment
outputs.constraints: No synthetic or omitted default endpoint; an exact input closure marker remains exactly once as the terminal vertex when end_coord is None

preconditions: Finite planar segment with meaningful polygon orientation
Any repeated closure endpoint matches the first vertex exactly
supported: Closed contours with an exact repeated start are re-closed without zero-length steps
Open untrimmed paths and nearest-end trimming remain supported
excluded: Non-exact repeated endpoints and general topology policies are not generalized

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError or the underlying NumPy/SciPy exception for nonfinite, mismatched, unsorted, out-of-domain, or malformed inputs; no input repair is inferred.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical, interpolation, or optional-dependency exceptions propagate from the direct calculation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation uses direct finite-difference, interpolation, selection, or quadrature operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is promised when input validation or the underlying numerical operation fails.

example.description: Parse a four-vertex contour segment while retaining its clockwise vertex order.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.sampling import parse_segment

segment = np.array([[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 0.0]])
np.testing.assert_array_equal(parse_segment(segment), segment)
example.expected: The four input vertices are returned in the same (4, 2) order.
